translationRepairs: He became friends across the generations with two eminent Sui veterans — Xue Daoheng, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Cui Zujun, Attendant Gentleman of the Household — and through them won a name for himself.

He became friends across the generations with two eminent Sui veterans — Xue Daoheng, Grand Master of the Capital Inspectors, and Cui Zujun, Imperial Diarist — and through them won a name for himself.
The source gives Xue Daoheng the Sui office 司隸大夫 and Cui Zujun 起居舍人, not the golden-seal grand-master or household-attendant ranks used in the original English.

The Sui officials Xue Daoheng, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Cui Zujun, Attendant Gentleman of the Household, were both veteran ministers of great standing; they became friends despite the age gap, and thereby he gained renown.

The Sui officials Xue Daoheng, Grand Master of the Capital Inspectors, and Cui Zujun, Imperial Diarist, were both veteran ministers of great standing; they became friends despite the age gap, and thereby he gained renown.
The same two offices are mistranslated in the literal English; 司隸大夫 and 起居舍人 are the capital-inspector grand master and the imperial diarist.

After Husizheng defected to Goguryeo, Shilian was punished for their association and demoted to registrar at Zhuyuan in Annam. His mother was too old to endure the southern climes, so he left his wife Xianyu to tend her and set out alone.

After Husizheng defected to Goguryeo, Shilian was punished for their association and demoted to registrar at Zhuyuan. His mother was too old to endure the southern miasmas, so he left his wife Xianyu to tend her and set out alone.
The sentence names only 硃鳶 and a 瘴癘地; Annam is an added gloss, and miasmas more faithfully render 瘴癘 than 'southern climes'.

In time he asked to retire. He was released from the vice directorship but given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Bag, made co-equal with the three departments at third rank, and kept in charge of state affairs.

In time he asked to retire. He was released from the vice directorship but given the dignity of opening an office with ceremonial equality to the Three Ministers, made a third-rank colleague of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and kept in charge of state affairs.
開府儀同三司 is ceremonial equality with the Three Ministers, not the golden-bag grand-master honorific, and 同中書門下三品 is third rank with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

After a long while he requested retirement; he was permitted to resign the vice directorship and was given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Bag, Co-equal with the Three Departments, Third Rank, and charge of state affairs.

After a long while he requested retirement; he was permitted to resign the vice directorship and was given the dignity of opening an office with ceremonial equality to the Three Ministers, third rank equal to the Secretariat and Chancellery, and charge of state affairs.
The literal line likewise replaces 開府儀同三司 with a golden-bag title the Chinese does not give, and misstates 同中書門下三品.
He demoted the Cui to third rank and had the register published empire-wide.
He then placed Cui Gan as the third surname and had the register published empire-wide.
The Chinese names 崔幹 as the third surname; the original English drops that personal name and treats the ranking as a clan-wide demotion of 'the Cui'.

Thereafter declining clans dropped from the registers, those not admitted in the line of descent all called themselves "forbidden-marriage houses," prized themselves all the more, and men and women secretly betrothed one another; the Son of Heaven could not forbid it — the age regarded it as a abuse.

Thereafter declining clans dropped from the registers, those not admitted in the line of descent all called themselves "forbidden-marriage houses," prized themselves all the more, and men and women secretly betrothed one another; the Son of Heaven could not forbid it — the age regarded it as an abuse.
The article in 'a abuse' is ungrammatical; 'an abuse' is the required correction of 世以為敝.
He was promoted to grand master of ceremonies for the crown prince.
He was promoted to supervisor of the household of the crown prince.
太子詹事 is the supervisor of the heir apparent's household, not the grand master of ceremonies (太常).
He was promoted to Grand Master of Ceremonies for the Crown Prince.
He was promoted to Supervisor of the Household of the Crown Prince.
The literal English makes the same 太子詹事 / 太常 confusion.

Whenever policy was debated he cited antiquity as instruction; the emperor grew still closer, once brought him into his private quarters, and said, "In antiquity Zhou had eight pillar states — your house and mine were among them.

Whenever policy was debated he cited antiquity as instruction; the emperor grew still closer, once brought him into his private quarters, and said, "In antiquity Zhou had eight pillars of state — your house and mine were among them.
八柱國 are the Eight Pillars of State, hereditary grandees, not 'pillar states'.

Whenever political gains and losses were discussed he cited antiquity as instruction; the emperor drew closer to him, once brought him into the inner sleeping quarters, and said, "In antiquity Zhou had eight pillar states — your house and mine were among them.

Whenever political gains and losses were discussed he cited antiquity as instruction; the emperor drew closer to him, once brought him into the inner sleeping quarters, and said, "In antiquity Zhou had eight pillars of state — your house and mine were among them.
The literal quotation repeats the same misreading of 八柱國 as territorial 'pillar states'.

Later, summoned to court, he was granted a seat in the imperial tower but sat without proper decorum; when again seated to receive an imperial message, the emperor in anger said, "When you went to Shu you all but wiped out the twenty mounted guards I gave you — my own Longzhong cavalry escort would scarcely be enough for you."

Later, summoned to court, he was granted a seat in the imperial tower but sat without proper decorum; when again seated to receive an imperial message, the emperor in anger said, "When you went to Shu you all but wiped out the twenty mounted guards I gave you — my own cavalry of Long stock would scarcely be enough for you."
隴種 is Long stock, not the place Longzhong; the proposed 'Long-stock cavalry' calque is still awkward, so the phrase is recast as 'cavalry of Long stock'.

Later he entered court; granted a seat in the imperial tower, his bearing was not respectful; again seated facing the edict, the Emperor angrily said: "When you entered Shu, the twenty mounted attendants of my carriage and fast-steed escorts — you executed nearly all of them; my Longzhong cavalry escort still would not suffice for you."

Later he entered court; granted a seat in the imperial tower, his bearing was not respectful; again seated facing the edict, the Emperor angrily said: "When you entered Shu, the twenty mounted attendants of my carriage and fast-steed escorts — you executed nearly all of them; my cavalry of Long stock still would not suffice for you."
The literal line has the same Longzhong error; 'Long-stock' is replaced with the more natural 'cavalry of Long stock' for 隴種.
The emperor was delighted, gave him ten fine horses, and sent him to seize the Wei south bank, capture Yongfeng Granary, raise five thousand troops, and help take the capital.
The emperor was delighted, gave him ten fine horses, and sent him to seize territory in Weinan, capture Yongfeng Granary, raise five thousand troops, and help take the capital.
渭南 is the place Weinan; 'Wei south bank' invents a riverbank the source does not name.
He was promoted to general of the left guards and awarded five hundred rolls of silk and goods.
He was promoted to grand general of the left commanding army and awarded five hundred rolls of silk and goods.
左領軍大將軍 is Grand General of the Left Commanding Army, not a general of the Left Guards (左衛).
He was transferred to General of the Left Guards and given five hundred rolls of goods.
He was transferred to Grand General of the Left Commanding Army and given five hundred rolls of goods.
The literal English likewise renders 左領軍 as Left Guards and omits that the rank is 大將軍.
His father Rongding served the Sui as military governor of Ming and duke of Chen, posthumously titled Majestic.
His father Rongding served the Sui as military governor of Ming and duke of Chen, posthumously titled Yi (Admirable).
諡曰懿 is the posthumous name Yi (Admirable), not Majestic.
As the Emperor's nephew he was early eminent; he entered the Imperial Academy and upon first appointment was made Palace Guard Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Bag.
As the Emperor's nephew he was early eminent; he entered the Imperial Academy and upon first appointment was made Palace Guard Attendant and Equal to the Three Dignitaries.
The appointment is 儀同三司, not 金紫光祿大夫; the golden-bag grand-master rank is invented.
When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, Emperor Yang suspected Kang might join him and sent Li Zixiong at full speed to relieve him of command.
When Liang, Prince of Han, rebelled, Emperor Yang suspected Kang might join him and sent Li Zixiong at full speed to relieve him of command.
漢王諒 is Liang, Prince of Han; 'Prince of Han Liang' fuses the title and the given name into one phrase.

Emperor Yang sent Kang to Lingwu to patrol the Great Wall. Learning Gaozu had taken the capital, Kang exclaimed with delight, "My kinsman by marriage is broad-minded and magnanimous — a true prince to restore order."

Emperor Yang sent Kang to Lingwu to patrol the Great Wall. Learning that Gaozu had taken the capital, Kang exclaimed with delight, "The son-in-law of our house is broad-minded and magnanimous — a true prince to restore order."
吾家婿 is specifically 'son-in-law of our house', and the participle needs a complement ('Learning that Gaozu').
He received a company of court musicians and treasures beyond reckoning.
He received a troupe of female musicians and treasures beyond reckoning.
女樂一部 specifies female musicians; 'court musicians' drops the sex of the troupe.
He also sowed discord among their tribes; the nine yishi chiefs including Yugu'ni under Yuju's division all submitted inward.
He also sowed discord among their tribes; the nine yishi chiefs including Yugu'ni under Yujue's division all submitted inward.
郁射 is Yujue in the idiomatic line and the extracted name; the literal 'Yuju' is an inconsistent romanization of the same person.

The emperor did not adopt the plan but praised Jing's loyalty and replied graciously: "I entrust all northern affairs to you. As Pacification Commissioner for the North, you leave me with no worry for that frontier."
The emperor did not adopt the plan but praised Jing's loyalty and replied graciously: "I entrust all northern affairs to you. As Ningshuo Commissioner, you leave me with no worry for that frontier."
甯朔大使 is the titled office Ningshuo Commissioner, not a generic 'Pacification Commissioner for the North'.
He died and was posthumously made minister of public works and governor of Jing, posthumously titled An.
He died and was posthumously made minister of public works and prefect of Jingzhou, posthumously titled An.
荊州刺史 is prefect of Jingzhou; 'governor of Jing' both misstates the office and collides with the personal name Jing.
His grandfather Zhao married Princess Yiyang of Northern Zhou and was enfeoffed duke of Julu.
His grandfather Zhao married Princess Yiyang, daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou, and was enfeoffed duke of Julu.
周文帝義陽公主 identifies Princess Yiyang as Emperor Wen of Zhou's daughter; the original keeps Northern Zhou but omits Emperor Wen.

Dexuan began as a thousand-bull officer in Gaozu's chancellor's office and remained relatively obscure through Taizong's reign. Honoring him as an old minister, Gaozong raised him from vice director of the palace department to censor-in-chief and within a year moved him to vice minister of revenue.

Dexuan began as a qianniu imperial bodyguard in Gaozu's chancellor's office and remained relatively obscure through Taizong's reign. Honoring him as an old minister, Gaozong raised him from vice director of the palace department to censor-in-chief and within a year moved him to vice minister of revenue.
千牛 is the qianniu bodyguard post; 'thousand-bull officer' is a misleading calque of the office name.
